title: WireGuard tunnel configs
whyItMatters: Each WireGuard config file holds the private key of a VPN tunnel and the peers it connects to. A copy of the file is enough to join the person's private network or to impersonate their machine.
source: wg-quick(8) reads <interface>.conf files from /etc/wireguard and creates the folder mode 0700: https://man.archlinux.org/man/wg-quick.8
notes: Root-only by design, hence requiresElevation. Configs can live elsewhere when a custom path is passed to wg-quick or the tunnel is managed by a desktop app, which keeps its own copy under the user's home; this rule only covers the system folder.

cleanup.signOut: Retire this machine's public keys on the WireGuard peers or gateways, so the tunnels no longer accept it.
steps: Remove the VPN connection in Settings > Network.
Leave the root-owned key files named in the plan to the full reset at the end of this plan.
cleanup.risk: The connection leaves Settings; the root-owned key files stay in the system folder until the full reset at the end of the plan.
